`IOWaitTimedOut`, `IOFailed` and `ServiceStopped`.

### The plan and refusals

The plan (`routines/plan.py`, `compile_plan`) names the routine (`command_routine`, `dataset`), what it was planned
for (`controller`, `motion_group`) and holds:

- `joint_trajectory`: the trajectory through all motions; location `n` is the start of motion `n` (locations count
  motions, not commands).
- `motions`: per motion command, in order, its index in `commands` and the `tcp` it moves with; entry `n` moves from
  location `n` to `n + 1`. Motions with different TCPs are not implemented yet (`501`), the shape allows them.
- `commands`: every other command, as authored (with its `at`, for display), and the `location` where it happens:
  the boundary of its place in the sequence, or where its `at` resolves to. A run uses `location`, never `at`.

An I/O-only routine has no `joint_trajectory`, `motion_group` or motions; all its commands are at location 0.

A run takes the plan as a `MotionPlan`, or as an `IOOnlyPlan` when it has no motions (`routines/plan.py`). Where
the robot stands follows from a `MotionPlan` (`MotionPlan.schedule`): at location 0, at the end, and at the location
of every `wait_for_io` / `wait_for_time`; there the service runs every command at that location in the routine's
order. Every other `set_io` is written by the controller as the robot passes it, a marker passes, and a
`pause_on_io` applies from its location to the end of the trajectory. A command with `at` that lands on a stop
(within 1e-6) runs at the stop, in order, written by the service. An `IOOnlyPlan` runs its commands in order.

A start refuses a plan that cannot run as it is with `422` `InvalidPlan`: a trajectory with a number that is not
finite, that does not run from 0 to the number of motions or whose locations decrease, a command off the
trajectory, a command index twice, a plan with motions without `controller`, `motion_group` or `joint_trajectory`,
an I/O-only plan with a `motion_group` or a `joint_trajectory` or with a command elsewhere than 0, or `CONTROLLER`
IOs without a `controller`. When the controller rejects the trajectory (`addTrajectory`: joint limit, collision,
torque, joint count, TCP), the `422` carries its report as `trajectory_error`, with `error_location_on_trajectory`
and the motion there as `command_index`; when NOVA refuses it as invalid data (HTTP 400 or 422), the `422` carries
NOVA's message. `409` when the controller reports an emergency stop or another safety stop (read before the start),
when NOVA refuses because the motion group is in use (HTTP 409), and as below; `502` only when NOVA cannot be
reached or fails.

Every refusal is a `CommandRoutineFailure`: a `code` (`CommandRoutineErrorCode`: `InvalidRequest`,
`InvalidRoutine`, `PlanningFailed`, `InvalidPlan`, `NotImplemented`, `NotFound`, `Conflict`, `Unreachable`), a
`message`, and `command_index` when it is about one command. A body that does not match the API is named field by field
(`body.commands: Field required`), without echoing it.
When a motion cannot be planned it also carries the planner's `error_feedback`, the `error_location_on_trajectory`
and the `joint_trajectory` up to there (the planner's partial trajectory, else the pieces planned before), on the
same location scale as `/plan`, so the reachable part can be drawn. A failure at the end of a motion (a cartesian
PTP fails at its target, location `k + 1`) is reported for that motion, not the next one.

### The routine against its motion group

Before planning, the service reads the description of the motion group on the request's `controller` (as the SDK
does): an unknown controller or motion group is `404`, start joints of the wrong length are `422`. The TCP the poses were taught with is the
ground truth: its offset is taken from the motion group (`tcps`) and replaces `motion_group_setup.tcp_offset` for
planning and kinematics, and the run executes with that TCP. A TCP the motion group does not have is `422`. A
request the motion planner itself refuses is `422` with only the planner's message.

With `motion_group_override` a motion routine moves that motion group of `controller` instead of its own, and is
planned with that motion group's setup, built from its description as the SDK's `MotionGroup.get_setup` builds it:
model, cycle time (8 ms if not described), mounting, `auto_limits`, the offset and safety colliders of the
routine's TCP, and the payload registered under that TCP's name. The routine's `motion_group_setup` is not used;
its start joints and poses are kept. An I/O-only routine ignores it.

### Following a run on NATS

Every change of a run (state, `current_command_index`, `error`) is published on
`nova.v2.cells.{cell}.command-routines.runs.{run}`, the same `CommandRoutineRun` that `GET .../runs/{run}` returns;
the last message of a run has a final state. Subscribe to `nova.v2.cells.{cell}.command-routines.runs.*` for every
run of the cell
(AsyncAPI in service-manager, `api/v2/routines/asyncapi.yaml`).

The service never stops reconnecting to NATS and logs every disconnect; a change it cannot publish while NATS is
away is logged as a warning (the run itself goes on, `GET` still has it). Should the connection still close for
good, `/healthz` answers `503`, so the pod is restarted.

Markers pass without effect for now; reporting them comes in a later change.

## How a routine is planned and its plan runs

- Only resolved routines are planned: every pose is an inline pose in the `world` frame. A run starts from a plan
  only; the plan is checked, and the controller has accepted its trajectory, before the start is answered; a
  refused start (`404`, `409`, `422`, `501`, `502`) moves nothing and writes nothing.
- The motions are planned into one trajectory, built from the routine (`routines/layout.py`,
  `routines/planning.py`); location `n` is the start of motion `n`, as `/plan` returns it. Consecutive
  explicit-path motions share one `planTrajectory` request and blend into each other; a generated motion and
  a boundary where the robot waits each start a new request (ADR 003/026), so the robot waits at the taught
  target, not on a blended path. The pieces are joined end to end. There the robot stops at the target: the
  blending of the motion before (own or inherited) is ignored and logged as a warning, not returned to the caller.
- Motion settings follow ADR 014: `blending` comes as a whole from the motion or the routine default
  (`null` = none); `limits_override` merges field by field (motion, then routine default, then the setup's
  `global_limits`; `null` skips the routine default). A generated motion takes no blending (spec §7.4): one
  that would inherit the routine's blending must set `blending: null`, else `422`.
  A run drives the plan's trajectory on the controller's `executeTrajectory` websocket itself
  (`routines/trajectory_execution.py`): it adds the trajectory to the controller's trajectory cache (which
  validates it), initializes it at its start, sends a `StartMovementRequest` to each location where the robot
  must stop, and removes the trajectory from the cache again once the run's final state is written (on its own,
  at most 10 s, so a slow controller delays neither the final state nor the next run). Arrival is read from the
  controller's state websocket, the only state that reports the trajectory (`execute`); the controller's state
  on NATS (`nova.v2.cells.{cell}.controllers.{controller}.state`) has none, so it serves the emergency stop only
  (`routines/controller_states.py`; without NATS the websocket serves it too). A controller that does not report
  the trajectory is judged by the joints: the robot stands at the target's joints after it has run. A motion not
  seen at its target within 8 times its planned duration plus 60 s fails the run. Every other command sits at the
  boundary between the motions around it (`routines/layout.py`), which is its `location` in the plan.
- The robot stops only before the first motion, after the last one, and where a `wait_for_time` or
  `wait_for_io` sits; there the service runs the commands at that location in order. A `set_io` between two
  motions without a wait travels with the trajectory and the controller writes it as the robot passes.
  A `marker` passes without effect.
- `wait_for_io` evaluates its whole expression (`all_of`, `any_of`, `not`, every comparator) on controller
  and bus IOs. Values are read over the API and pushed over NATS while the wait lasts: bus IOs from
  `nova.v2.cells.{cell}.bus-ios.ios`, controller IOs on a per-wait subscription
  (`...controllers.{controller}.ios.subscribe`, renewed and cancelled). Without NATS, or when a subscription
  is refused, they are polled every 100 ms (`routines/ios.py`).

### The plan and refusals

The plan (`routines/plan.py`, `compile_plan`) names the routine (`command_routine`, `dataset`), what it was planned
for (`controller`, `motion_group`) and holds:

- `joint_trajectory`: the trajectory through all motions; location `n` is the start of motion `n` (locations count
  motions, not commands).
- `motions`: per motion command, in order, its index in `commands` and the `tcp` it moves with; entry `n` moves from
  location `n` to `n + 1`. Motions with different TCPs are not implemented yet (`501`), the shape allows them.
- `commands`: every other command, as authored (with its `at`, for display), and the `location` where it happens:
  the boundary of its place in the sequence, or where its `at` resolves to. A run uses `location`, never `at`.

An I/O-only routine has no `joint_trajectory`, `motion_group` or motions; all its commands are at location 0.

A run takes the plan as a `MotionPlan`, or as an `IOOnlyPlan` when it has no motions (`routines/plan.py`). Where
the robot stands follows from a `MotionPlan` (`MotionPlan.schedule`): at location 0, at the end, and at the location
of every `wait_for_io` / `wait_for_time`; there the service runs every command at that location in the routine's
order. Every other `set_io` is written by the controller as the robot passes it, a marker passes, and a
`pause_on_io` applies from its location to the end of the trajectory. A command with `at` that lands on a stop
(within 1e-6) runs at the stop, in order, written by the service. An `IOOnlyPlan` runs its commands in order.

A start refuses a plan that cannot run as it is with `422` `InvalidPlan`: a trajectory with a number that is not
finite, that does not run from 0 to the number of motions or whose locations decrease, a command off the
trajectory, a command index twice, a plan with motions without `controller`, `motion_group` or `joint_trajectory`,
an I/O-only plan with a `motion_group` or a `joint_trajectory` or with a command elsewhere than 0, or `CONTROLLER`
IOs without a `controller`. When the controller rejects the trajectory (`addTrajectory`: joint limit, collision,
torque, joint count, TCP), the `422` carries its report as `trajectory_error`, with `error_location_on_trajectory`
and the motion there as `command_index`; when NOVA refuses it as invalid data (HTTP 400 or 422), the `422` carries
NOVA's message. `409` when the controller reports an emergency stop or another safety stop (read before the start),
when NOVA refuses because the motion group is in use (HTTP 409), and as below; `502` only when NOVA cannot be
reached or fails.

Every refusal is a `CommandRoutineFailure`: a `code` (`CommandRoutineErrorCode`: `InvalidRequest`,
`InvalidRoutine`, `PlanningFailed`, `InvalidPlan`, `NotImplemented`, `NotFound`, `Conflict`, `Unreachable`), a
`message`, and `command_index` when it is about one command. A body that does not match the API is named field by field
(`body.commands: Field required`), without echoing it.
When a motion cannot be planned it also carries the planner's `error_feedback`, the `error_location_on_trajectory`
and the `joint_trajectory` up to there (the planner's partial trajectory, else the pieces planned before), on the
same location scale as `/plan`, so the reachable part can be drawn. A failure at the end of a motion (a cartesian
PTP fails at its target, location `k + 1`) is reported for that motion, not the next one.

Before planning, the service reads the description of the motion group on the request's `controller` (as the SDK
does): an unknown controller or motion group is `404`, start joints of the wrong length are `422`. The TCP the poses were taught with is the
ground truth: its offset is taken from the motion group (`tcps`) and replaces `motion_group_setup.tcp_offset` for
planning and kinematics, and the run executes with that TCP. A TCP the motion group does not have is `422`. A
request the motion planner itself refuses is `422` with only the planner's message.

"""Runs of command routines: planning a routine, starting the run of a plan, tracking and stopping it.

``plan`` returns the executable plan of a routine (``routines.plan``); a run executes such a plan as it is and
never plans again. A plan is checked, and the controller has accepted its trajectory, before its start is
answered, so every rejection happens before the robot moves. The run then executes in the background
(``Execution``); its state is kept in the memory of the service (``RunStore``) until it restarts, and every
change is published on NATS.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import contextlib
import json
import logging
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Coroutine
from typing import Any, TypeVar

import nats
from nova import api
from nova.core.gateway import ApiGateway
from wandelbots_api_client.v2_pydantic.exceptions import ApiException, NotFoundException

from routines.api import models
from routines.api.models import CommandRoutineRun, CommandRoutineRunState
from routines.errors import Conflict, InvalidPlan, NotFound, Rejected, Unreachable
from routines.controller_states import ControllerStates
from routines.execution import Execution, IOOnlyExecution, MotionExecution, StepFailed
from routines.ios import IOConditionTimedOut, IOs
from routines.layout import lay_out
from routines.plan import ExecutionPlan, IOOnlyPlan, MotionPlan, compile_plan, execution_plan
from routines.planning import Planner, api_message
from routines.trajectory_execution import StartRefused

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

T = TypeVar("T")


PREPARING = CommandRoutineRunState("PREPARING")
RUNNING = CommandRoutineRunState("RUNNING")
COMPLETED = CommandRoutineRunState("COMPLETED")
FAILED = CommandRoutineRunState("FAILED")
STOPPED = CommandRoutineRunState("STOPPED")
FINAL = (COMPLETED, FAILED, STOPPED)

# The robot's location in the run state is updated at most this often [s].
PROGRESS_INTERVAL = 0.1
# How long a stop waits for the execution to stop the run.
STOP_TIMEOUT = 10.0
_STOP_POLL_INTERVAL = 0.05


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunFailure:
    """Why a run failed: the readable ``message`` and its typed ``cause``."""

    message: str
    cause: models.CommandRoutineFailureCause


class RunStore:
    """The runs of the service, in memory: a restart forgets them."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._runs: dict[str, CommandRoutineRun] = {}
        self._stops: dict[str, asyncio.Event] = {}
        self._failures: dict[str, RunFailure] = {}

    def _stop_event(self, run: str) -> asyncio.Event:
        return self._stops.setdefault(run, asyncio.Event())

    async def request_stop(self, run: str, failure: RunFailure | None = None) -> None:
        """Ask the execution of ``run`` to stop it: ``STOPPED``, or ``FAILED`` with ``failure`` as its error.

        The first request decides.
        """
        event = self._stop_event(run)
        if not event.is_set() and failure is not None:
            self._failures[run] = failure
        event.set()

    async def wait_for_stop(self, run: str) -> None:
        """Return once a stop of ``run`` was requested, also before this call."""
        await self._stop_event(run).wait()

    def stop_failure(self, run: str) -> RunFailure | None:
        """Why the requested stop fails ``run``; ``None`` for a stop that leaves it ``STOPPED``."""
        return self._failures.get(run)

    async def put(self, run: CommandRoutineRun) -> None:
        self._runs[run.run] = run.model_copy()

    async def get(self, run: str) -> CommandRoutineRun | None:
        stored = self._runs.get(run)
        return None if stored is None else stored.model_copy()

    async def all_runs(self) -> list[CommandRoutineRun]:
        return [run.model_copy() for run in self._runs.values()]


def _cause(error: BaseException) -> str:
    """The innermost message of an error raised from task groups."""
    error = _innermost(error)
    return str(error) or type(error).__name__


def _innermost(error: BaseException) -> BaseException:
    while isinstance(error, BaseExceptionGroup) and error.exceptions:
        error = error.exceptions[0]
    return error


def _failure_cause(error: BaseException) -> models.CommandRoutineFailureCause:
    """The ``CommandRoutineFailureCause`` of an error that failed a started run.

    A command that is not a motion fails on its IOs; everything else is the motion.
    """
    inner = _innermost(error)
    if isinstance(inner, StepFailed):
        timed_out = isinstance(inner.__cause__, IOConditionTimedOut)
        return models.CommandRoutineFailureCause("IOWaitTimedOut" if timed_out else "IOFailed")
    return models.CommandRoutineFailureCause("MotionFailed")


async def _first_of(**awaitables: Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]) -> str:
    """Run ``awaitables`` until the first one ends, cancel the others and return its name.

    Of several that end together, the one given first wins. Cancelling the execution closes
    its connection to the controller, which stops the motion. An error of the one that ends
    is raised.
    """
    tasks = {asyncio.ensure_future(awaitable): name for name, awaitable in awaitables.items()}
    try:
        done, _ = await asyncio.wait(tasks, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
    finally:
        for task in tasks:
            task.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
    first = next(task for task in tasks if task in done)
    first.result()
    return tasks[first]


_ESTOP_CAUSE = "The run was ended by an emergency stop"
_ESTOP_REFUSAL = "The controller reports an emergency stop or another safety stop"
_ESTOP = models.CommandRoutineFailureCause("EmergencyStop")
# As the program runner: every other safety state stops the robot.
_SAFE_STATES = (api.models.SafetyStateType.SAFETY_STATE_NORMAL, api.models.SafetyStateType.SAFETY_STATE_REDUCED)


def _is_estop(state: api.models.RobotControllerState) -> bool:
    return state.safety_state not in _SAFE_STATES


def _activity(state: api.models.MotionGroupState) -> str | None:
    """What NOVA is doing with the motion group, if it is busy."""
    execute = state.execute
    if execute is None or execute.details is None:
        return None
    details = execute.details
    if isinstance(details, api.models.JoggingDetails):
        return "jogging is active"
    if isinstance(details.state, api.models.TrajectoryEnded):
        return None
    return f"trajectory '{details.trajectory}' is being executed"


class RunPublisher:
    """Publishes every change of a run on ``{instance}.v2.cells.{cell}.command-routines.runs.{run}``."""

    def __init__(self, client: nats.NATS | None, cell: str):
        self._client = client
        self._cell = cell

    def subject(self, run: str) -> str:
        return f"nova.v2.cells.{self._cell}.command-routines.runs.{run}"

    async def publish(self, run: CommandRoutineRun) -> None:
        if self._client is None:
            return
        if not self._client.is_connected:
            logger.warning(f"Run {run.run} ({run.state.root}) not published: NATS is not connected")
            return
        try:
            await self._client.publish(self.subject(run.run), run.model_dump_json(exclude_none=True).encode())
        except Exception:  # the run is in the store; a lost event must not fail the run
            logger.exception(f"Publishing run {run.run} failed")


def _now() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc)


def _location(run: CommandRoutineRun) -> float | None:
    return None if run.current_location is None else run.current_location.root


class _Report:
    """Writes what an execution does to its run in the store and publishes every change on NATS."""

    def __init__(self, store: RunStore, run: CommandRoutineRun, publisher: RunPublisher):
        self._store = store
        self._publisher = publisher
        self.run = run
        self.accepted = asyncio.Event()
        self.as_accepted = run

124	        if self.motion_group_override is not None:

135	    def holds_at(self, boundary: int) -> bool:
136	        """Whether the robot stands still at ``boundary`` while the service runs its steps in order.
137	
138	        It does before the first and after the last motion, and wherever a step waits. At every
139	        other boundary the robot moves on, and the controller writes the outputs on the way.
140	        """
141	        if boundary in (0, self.end):
142	            return True
143	        return any(isinstance(step.command, _HOLDING) for step in self.boundaries[boundary])
144	
145	    def pieces(self) -> list[list[Movement]]:
146	        """The motions planned in one request each.
147	
148	        Consecutive explicit-path motions are planned together, so they blend into each other; every
149	        generated motion on its own. A boundary where the robot holds (a wait) ends a piece
150	        too (ADR 003/026): the robot stops at the taught target of the motion before it.
151	        """
152	        pieces: list[list[Movement]] = []
153	        for k, movement in enumerate(self.movements):
154	            joins = (
155	                isinstance(movement.motion, PathMotion)
156	                and pieces
157	                and isinstance(pieces[-1][-1].motion, PathMotion)
158	                and not self.holds_at(k)
159	            )
160	            if joins:
161	                pieces[-1].append(movement)
162	            else:
163	                pieces.append([movement])

166	    @property
167	    def warnings(self) -> list[str]:
168	        """What the routine asks for but does not get: blending of a motion where the robot has to stop.
169	
170	        A piece is planned on its own, so its last motion cannot blend into the next one: the robot stops
171	        at its target and its blending, set on the motion or inherited from the routine's defaults, is
172	        ignored. The routine's last motion has nothing to blend into anyway.
173	        """
174	        warnings = []
175	        pieces = self.pieces()
176	        for i in range(len(pieces) - 1):
177	            reason = self._stop_reason(i)
178	            if reason is not None:
179	                last = pieces[i][-1]
180	                warnings.append(
181	                    f"Command {last.index} (motion_command): its blending is ignored, the robot stops at its "
182	                    f"target because {reason}"
183	                )
184	        return warnings

186	    def _stop_reason(self, piece: int) -> str | None:
187	        """Why the robot stops after ``piece`` although its last motion blends; ``None`` if it does not blend."""
188	        pieces = self.pieces()
189	        last, following = pieces[piece][-1], pieces[piece + 1][0]
190	        if _blending_of(last.motion) is None:
191	            return None
192	        boundary = self.movements.index(following)
193	        holding = [step for step in self.boundaries[boundary] if isinstance(step.command, _HOLDING)]
194	        if holding:
195	            return f"command {holding[0].index} ({holding[0].command.type}) waits there"
196	        return f"command {following.index} (motion_command) with a generated path is planned on its own"

201	        return any(
202	            item.command.at is not None and isinstance(item.command.at.root, models.DistanceTrigger)
203	            for item in self.triggered
204	        )

207	def lay_out(
208	    routine: models.CommandRoutine, controller: str | None = None, motion_group_override: str | None = None
209	) -> CommandRoutineLayout:
210	    """Check that the service can run ``routine`` on ``controller`` and lay out its commands.
211	
212	    A motion routine moves ``motion_group_override``, if given, else its own motion group; both are motion groups
213	    of ``controller``. An I/O-only routine addresses the ``CONTROLLER`` IOs of ``controller`` and ignores
214	    ``motion_group_override``.
215	
216	    Raises:
217	        InvalidRoutine: The routine is not resolved or lacks its context.
218	        NotImplementedYet: The routine uses a feature the service does not implement yet.
219	        Both are raised before NOVA is asked anything.
220	    """
221	    check_resolved(routine)
222	    io_only = routine.motion_group_setup is None
223	    if not io_only:
224	        _check_context(routine, controller)
225	    else:
226	        _check_io_only_context(routine)
227	        motion_group_override = None
228	    tcp = None if io_only else _tcp(routine)
229	
230	    movements: list[Movement] = []
231	    boundaries: list[list[Step]] = [[]]
232	    triggered: list[Triggered] = []
233	    for index, wrapped in enumerate(routine.commands):
234	        command = wrapped.root
235	        label = f"Command {index} ({command.type})"
236	        if isinstance(command, (models.ExplicitPathMotionCommand, models.GeneratedPathMotionCommand)):
237	            if io_only:
238	                raise InvalidRoutine(
239	                    f"{label}: an I/O-only routine, without a motion group setup, cannot move", command_index=index
240	                )
241	            with _about(index):
242	                movements.append(Movement(index, _motion(routine, label, command)))
243	            boundaries.append([])
244	            continue
245	        if io_only and controller is None:
246	            with _about(index):
247	                _check_io_only_origin(label, command)
248	        if command.at is not None and movements:
249	            triggered.append(Triggered(index, command, anchor=len(movements) - 1))
250	        else:
251	            # Without a preceding motion (also in an I/O-only routine) an `at` trigger has no motion to anchor to:
252	            # it collapses to the start (spec §8.2), and the command runs at its place in the sequence.
253	            boundaries[-1].append(Step(index, command))
254	
255	    if not io_only and not movements:
256	        raise InvalidRoutine("A routine with a motion group setup needs at least one motion command")
257	    return CommandRoutineLayout(
258	        routine=routine,
259	        movements=tuple(movements),
260	        boundaries=tuple(tuple(steps) for steps in boundaries),
261	        triggered=tuple(triggered),
262	        tcp=tcp,
263	        controller=controller,
264	        motion_group_override=motion_group_override,
265	    )

1	"""Planning a routine's motions into one trajectory, without moving the robot.
2	
3	Consecutive motions along explicit paths are planned in one ``planTrajectory`` request, so they
4	blend into each other. A generated (collision-free) motion is planned on its own, from where the
5	motions before it end, as the SDK plans collision-free motions in an action list: a pose target is
6	turned into joints by inverse kinematics, and ``planCollisionFree`` generates the path. A wait also
7	ends a piece (ADR 003/026).
8	
9	The pieces are joined end to end; location ``k`` stays the start of motion ``k``.
10	
11	The motion group's description on its controller decides what the routine's setup cannot: that the motion group
12	exists, how many joints it has, and the offset of the TCP the routine's poses were taught with. That TCP is the
13	ground truth (decision 26); its offset replaces the setup's ``tcp_offset``, as the SDK takes it from the
14	description too. A routine moved to another motion group (the request's ``motion_group_override``) is planned
15	with that motion group's whole setup from its description instead of the routine's.
16	
17	When a motion cannot be planned, the refusal (``PlanningFailed``) names its command and carries what the planner
18	reports, on the routine's location scale: its feedback, where planning failed and the trajectory up to there.
19	"""

67	    async def plan(self, layout: CommandRoutineLayout) -> api.models.JointTrajectory | None:
68	        """The trajectory through all motions of ``layout`` from its start joints; ``None`` for an I/O-only one.
69	
70	        It is planned with the routine's own context: motion group setup (or, with ``motion_group_override``,
71	        that motion group's), TCP, start joints and motion settings. The same request always yields the
72	        trajectory a run executes.
73	
74	        Raises:
75	            InvalidRoutine: The routine does not fit the motion group (joints, TCP), or the planner refuses it.
76	            PlanningFailed: A motion cannot be planned; the error names its command.
77	            NotFound: NOVA does not know the motion group or its controller.
78	            Unreachable: The motion planner failed or could not be reached.
79	        """
80	        if layout.io_only:
81	            return None
82	        for warning in layout.warnings:
83	            # Logged only, not part of the API response.
84	            logger.warning(f"Routine '{layout.routine.command_routine.root}': {warning}")
85	        routine = layout.routine
86	        assert routine.start_joint_position is not None
87	        setup = await self.setup(layout)
88	        joints = list(routine.start_joint_position.root)
89	        pieces: list[api.models.JointTrajectory] = []
90	        start = 0  # the location where the piece starts: the number of motions before it
91	        try:
92	            for piece in layout.pieces():
93	                try:
94	                    trajectory = await self._plan_piece(setup, joints, piece)
95	                except _PieceFailed as failed:
96	                    raise _planning_failed(piece[failed.motion], failed, start, pieces) from None
97	                pieces.append(trajectory)
98	                joints = list(trajectory.joint_positions[-1])
99	                start += len(piece)
100	        except NotFoundException as error:
101	            raise NotFound(f"Motion group '{layout.motion_group}' not found: {api_message(error)}") from error
102	        except ApiException as error:
103	            if error.status is not None and 400 <= error.status < 500:
104	                raise InvalidRoutine(f"The motion planner refused the routine: {api_message(error)}") from error
105	            raise Unreachable(f"Planning the routine failed: {api_message(error)}") from error
106	        except OSError as error:
107	            raise Unreachable(f"The motion planner could not be reached: {error}") from error
108	        return _joined(pieces)

112

"""Planning a routine's motions into one trajectory, without moving the robot.

Consecutive motions along explicit paths are planned in one ``planTrajectory`` request, so they
blend into each other. A generated (collision-free) motion is planned on its own, from where the
motions before it end, as the SDK plans collision-free motions in an action list: a pose target is
turned into joints by inverse kinematics, and ``planCollisionFree`` generates the path. A wait also
ends a piece (ADR 003/026).

The pieces are joined end to end; location ``k`` stays the start of motion ``k``.

The motion group's description on its controller decides what the routine's setup cannot: that the motion group
exists, how many joints it has, and the offset of the TCP the routine's poses were taught with. That TCP is the
ground truth (decision 26); its offset replaces the setup's ``tcp_offset``, as the SDK takes it from the
description too. A routine moved to another motion group (the request's ``motion_group_override``) is planned
with that motion group's whole setup from its description instead of the routine's.

When a motion cannot be planned, the refusal (``PlanningFailed``) names its command and carries what the planner
reports, on the routine's location scale: its feedback, where planning failed and the trajectory up to there.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from collections.abc import Sequence
from dataclasses import dataclass
from math import ceil
from typing import Any

from nova import api
from nova.cell.motion_group import _find_and_sort_best_joint_solutions
from nova.core.gateway import ApiGateway
from nova.utils.joint_trajectory import combine_trajectories
from nova.utils.motion_group_setup import (
    get_joint_position_limits_from_motion_group_setup,
    motion_group_setup_from_motion_group_description,
)
from wandelbots_api_client.v2_pydantic.exceptions import ApiException, NotFoundException

from routines.api import models
from routines.errors import InvalidRoutine, NotFound, PlanningFailed, Unreachable
from routines.kinematics import folded_limits
from routines.layout import CommandRoutineLayout, GeneratedMotion, Movement, PathMotion, unblended

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclass
class _PieceFailed(Exception):
    """A motion of a piece cannot be planned; locations count from the start of the piece."""

    motion: int
    """The position of the motion in the piece."""
    reason: str
    """Follows the command's label in the message."""
    location: float
    partial: api.models.JointTrajectory | None = None
    """The planner's trajectory from the start of the piece to the error."""
    feedback: Any = None


class Planner:
    def __init__(self, gateway: ApiGateway, cell: str):
        self._gateway = gateway
        self._cell = cell

    async def plan(self, layout: CommandRoutineLayout) -> api.models.JointTrajectory | None:
        """The trajectory through all motions of ``layout`` from its start joints; ``None`` for an I/O-only one.

        It is planned with the routine's own context: motion group setup (or, with ``motion_group_override``,
        that motion group's), TCP, start joints and motion settings. The same request always yields the
        trajectory a run executes.

        Raises:
            InvalidRoutine: The routine does not fit the motion group (joints, TCP), or the planner refuses it.
            PlanningFailed: A motion cannot be planned; the error names its command.
            NotFound: NOVA does not know the motion group or its controller.
            Unreachable: The motion planner failed or could not be reached.
        """
        if layout.io_only:
            return None
        for warning in layout.warnings:
            # Logged only, not part of the API response.
            logger.warning(f"Routine '{layout.routine.command_routine.root}': {warning}")
        routine = layout.routine
        assert routine.start_joint_position is not None
        setup = await self.setup(layout)
        joints = list(routine.start_joint_position.root)
        pieces: list[api.models.JointTrajectory] = []
        start = 0  # the location where the piece starts: the number of motions before it
        try:
            for piece in layout.pieces():
                try:
                    trajectory = await self._plan_piece(setup, joints, piece)
                except _PieceFailed as failed:
                    raise _planning_failed(piece[failed.motion], failed, start, pieces) from None
                pieces.append(trajectory)
                joints = list(trajectory.joint_positions[-1])
                start += len(piece)
        except NotFoundException as error:
            raise NotFound(f"Motion group '{layout.motion_group}' not found: {api_message(error)}") from error
        except ApiException as error:
            if error.status is not None and 400 <= error.status < 500:
                raise InvalidRoutine(f"The motion planner refused the routine: {api_message(error)}") from error
            raise Unreachable(f"Planning the routine failed: {api_message(error)}") from error
        except OSError as error:
            raise Unreachable(f"The motion planner could not be reached: {error}") from error
        return _joined(pieces)

    async def setup(self, layout: CommandRoutineLayout) -> api.models.MotionGroupSetup:
        """The setup the routine is planned with, checked against the motion group it moves.

        Without an override it is the routine's own setup with the offset of its TCP on the motion group. With
        ``motion_group_override`` it is the setup of that motion group as NOVA describes it, built as the SDK
        builds it (``MotionGroup.get_setup``): model, cycle time, mounting, limits, the offset and safety colliders of
        the routine's TCP, and the payload registered under that TCP's name.

        Raises:
            NotFound: The motion group, or its controller, does not exist.
            InvalidRoutine: The start joints do not fit the motion group, or it has no TCP of the poses' name.
            Unreachable: NOVA failed or could not be reached.
        """
        routine = layout.routine
        assert routine.motion_group_setup is not None and routine.start_joint_position is not None
        controller = layout.motion_controller
        try:
            description = await self._gateway.motion_group_api.get_motion_group_description(
                cell=self._cell, controller=controller, motion_group=layout.motion_group
            )
        except NotFoundException as error:
            raise NotFound(
                f"Motion group '{layout.motion_group}' not found on controller '{controller}': {api_message(error)}"
            ) from error
        except ApiException as error:
            raise Unreachable(f"Reading motion group '{layout.motion_group}' failed: {api_message(error)}") from error
        except OSError as error:
            raise Unreachable(f"NOVA could not be reached: {error}") from error
        limits = description.operation_limits.auto_limits
        dof = len(limits.joints) if limits is not None and limits.joints else None
        given = len(routine.start_joint_position.root)
        if dof is not None and given != dof:
            raise InvalidRoutine(
                f"Routine '{routine.command_routine.root}': start_joint_position has {given} joints, "
                f"but motion group '{layout.motion_group}' has {dof}"
            )
        tcps = description.tcps or {}
        if layout.tcp is not None and layout.tcp not in tcps:
            raise InvalidRoutine(
                f"Routine '{routine.command_routine.root}': the poses were taught with the TCP '{layout.tcp}', "
                f"but motion group '{layout.motion_group}' has no such TCP (it has: {', '.join(sorted(tcps)) or 'none'})"
            )
        if layout.motion_group_override is not None:
            if limits is None:
                raise Unreachable(f"Motion group '{layout.motion_group}' reports no limits to plan with")
            payloads = description.payloads or {}
            return motion_group_setup_from_motion_group_description(
                description, tcp_name=layout.tcp, payload=payloads.get(layout.tcp) if layout.tcp else None
            )
        setup = api.models.MotionGroupSetup.model_validate(
            routine.motion_group_setup.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True)
        )
        if layout.tcp is None:
            return setup  # no poses and no tcp: only joint motions, the TCP does not change the path
        return setup.model_copy(update={"tcp_offset": tcps[layout.tcp].pose})

    async def tcp_positions(
        self, layout: CommandRoutineLayout, trajectory: api.models.JointTrajectory
    ) -> list[list[float]]:
        """The TCP position [mm] at every sample of ``trajectory``, for triggers by distance."""
        setup = await self.setup(layout)
        try:
            poses = await self._kinematics(setup).forward(self._cell, trajectory.joint_positions)
        except ApiException as error:
            raise Unreachable(f"Forward kinematics of the trajectory failed: {api_message(error)}") from error
        return [list(pose.position or (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)) for pose in poses]

    async def _plan_piece(
        self, setup: api.models.MotionGroupSetup, joints: list[float], piece: list[Movement]
    ) -> api.models.JointTrajectory:
        first = piece[0].motion
        if isinstance(first, GeneratedMotion):
            return await self._plan_generated(setup, joints, piece[0], first)
        commands = [movement.motion.command for movement in piece if isinstance(movement.motion, PathMotion)]
        # Nothing follows within the request: the robot stops at the target (see CommandRoutineLayout.warnings).
        commands[-1] = unblended(commands[-1])
        response = await self._gateway.trajectory_planning_api.plan_trajectory(
            cell=self._cell,
            plan_trajectory_request=api.models.PlanTrajectoryRequest(
                motion_group_setup=setup,
                start_joint_position=joints,
                motion_commands=commands,
                singularity_handling=api.models.SingularityHandling.NONE,
            ),
        )
        result = response.response
        if isinstance(result, api.models.PlanTrajectoryFailedResponse):
            location = result.error_location_on_trajectory or 0.0
            # Motion k runs from location k to k + 1: a location at its end (where a PTP fails at its
            # target) still belongs to it, not to the next one.
            motion = min(max(ceil(location) - 1, 0), len(piece) - 1)
            feedback = _feedback(result)
            raise _PieceFailed(
                motion,
                f" cannot be planned: {_name(feedback)}",
                location,
                partial=result.joint_trajectory,
                feedback=feedback,
            )
        return result

    async def _plan_generated(
        self, setup: api.models.MotionGroupSetup, joints: list[float], movement: Movement, motion: GeneratedMotion
    ) -> api.models.JointTrajectory:
        limits = setup.global_limits
        try:
            global_limits = folded_limits(limits, motion.limits_override)
        except ValueError as error:
            raise InvalidRoutine(
                f"Command {movement.index} (motion_command): {error}", command_index=movement.index
            ) from error
        if isinstance(motion.target, api.models.Pose):
            [solutions] = await self._kinematics(setup).inverse(self._cell, [motion.target])
            if not solutions:
                raise _PieceFailed(0, ": the target cannot be reached, no inverse kinematics solution", 0.0)
            # Turned close to the start and sorted nearest first, as the SDK plans a collision-free motion.
            targets = _find_and_sort_best_joint_solutions(
                tuple(joints),
                [tuple(solution) for solution in solutions],
                limits.joints if limits is not None else None,
            )
        else:
            targets = [motion.target]
        request_setup = setup.model_copy(update={"global_limits": global_limits})
        failure: api.models.PlanCollisionFreeFailedResponse | None = None
        for target in targets:
            response = await self._gateway.trajectory_planning_api.plan_collision_free(
                cell=self._cell,
                plan_collision_free_request=api.models.PlanCollisionFreeRequest(
                    motion_group_setup=request_setup,
                    start_joint_position=joints,
                    target=list(target),
                    constraint=motion.constraint,
                    algorithm=motion.algorithm,
                ),
            )
            if isinstance(response.response, api.models.JointTrajectory):
                return _one_motion(response.response)
            failure = response.response
        feedback = _feedback(failure) if failure is not None else None
        reason = _name(feedback) if feedback is not None else "no target joints"
        raise _PieceFailed(0, f": no collision-free path was found: {reason}", 0.0, feedback=feedback)

    def _kinematics(self, setup: api.models.MotionGroupSetup) -> _Kinematics:
        return _Kinematics(self._gateway, setup)


class _Kinematics:
    """Forward and inverse kinematics of the routine's motion group setup, with its TCP and mounting."""

    def __init__(self, gateway: ApiGateway, setup: api.models.MotionGroupSetup):
        self._gateway = gateway
        self._setup = setup

    async def forward(self, cell: str, joints: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> list[api.models.Pose]:
        response = await self._gateway.kinematics_api.forward_kinematics(
            cell=cell,
            forward_kinematics_request=api.models.ForwardKinematicsRequest(
                motion_group_model=self._setup.motion_group_model,
                joint_positions=[list(sample) for sample in joints],
                tcp_offset=self._setup.tcp_offset,
                mounting=self._setup.mounting,
            ),
        )
        return list(response.tcp_poses)

    async def inverse(self, cell: str, poses: list[api.models.Pose]) -> list[list[list[float]]]:
        response = await self._gateway.kinematics_api.inverse_kinematics(
            cell=cell,
            inverse_kinematics_request=api.models.InverseKinematicsRequest(
                motion_group_model=self._setup.motion_group_model,
                tcp_poses=poses,
                tcp_offset=self._setup.tcp_offset,
                mounting=self._setup.mounting,
                joint_position_limits=get_joint_position_limits_from_motion_group_setup(self._setup),
                collision_setups=self._setup.collision_setups,
            ),
        )
        return [[list(solution) for solution in solutions] for solutions in response.joints]


def _one_motion(trajectory: api.models.JointTrajectory) -> api.models.JointTrajectory:
    """A generated path as one motion: its locations scaled to run from 0 to 1."""
    end = trajectory.locations[-1] or 1.0
    return trajectory.model_copy(update={"locations": [location / end for location in trajectory.locations]})


def _joined(pieces: list[api.models.JointTrajectory]) -> api.models.JointTrajectory:
    """The pieces end to end: each continues the times and locations where the previous one ended."""
    # The SDK extends the first trajectory in place; it is copied so the planned pieces stay as planned.
    return combine_trajectories([pieces[0].model_copy(deep=True), *pieces[1:]])


def _planning_failed(
    movement: Movement, failed: _PieceFailed, start: int, pieces: list[api.models.JointTrajectory]
) -> PlanningFailed:
    """The refusal of the routine: ``failed`` placed on its trajectory, after the ``pieces`` planned before."""
    reached = list(pieces)
    if failed.partial is not None and failed.partial.joint_positions:
        reached.append(failed.partial)
    trajectory = _joined(reached).model_dump(mode="json") if reached else None
    return PlanningFailed(
        f"Command {movement.index} (motion_command){failed.reason}",
        command_index=movement.index,
        location=start + failed.location,
        trajectory=trajectory,
        feedback=failed.feedback,
    )


def _feedback(
    failure: api.models.PlanTrajectoryFailedResponse | api.models.PlanCollisionFreeFailedResponse,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The planner's feedback as the API returns it (``error_feedback_name`` names its kind)."""
    feedback = getattr(failure.error_feedback, "root", failure.error_feedback)
    return feedback.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True)


def _name(feedback: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    return feedback.get("error_feedback_name", "unknown planner error")


def api_message(error: ApiException) -> str:
    """The message of NOVA's error response, not the whole response."""
    data = getattr(error, "data", None)
    message = getattr(data, "message", None)
    if message:
        return message
    try:
        body = json.loads(error.body or "")
    except ValueError:
        return (error.body or str(error.reason))[:500]
    if isinstance(body, dict):
        detail = body.get("message") or body.get("detail")
        if isinstance(detail, list):  # a validation error: each problem as `where: what`
            return "; ".join(
                f"{'.'.join(str(part) for part in item.get('loc', ()))}: {item.get('msg', 'invalid')}"
                for item in detail
                if isinstance(item, dict)
            )
        if detail:
            return str(detail)
    return str(error.reason)

133	    its connection to the controller, which stops the motion. An error of the one that ends

491	                    ),

508

510	        delays neither the final state nor a next run on the motion group.
511	        """

519

521	            Rejected: Why the start is refused, when the run ended before it was accepted.
522	        """
523	        run = report.run.run
524	        watched: dict[str, Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]] = {
525	            "execution": execution.run(report),

527	        }

535	                    FAILED,
536	                    RunFailure(

538	                        models.CommandRoutineFailureCause("ServiceStopped"),
539	                    ),
540	                )
541	            raise
542	        except Exception as error:  # every failure of a run is reported in its state

"""Runs of command routines: planning a routine, starting the run of a plan, tracking and stopping it.

``plan`` returns the executable plan of a routine (``routines.plan``); a run executes such a plan as it is and
never plans again. A plan is checked, and the controller has accepted its trajectory, before its start is
answered, so every rejection happens before the robot moves. The run then executes in the background
(``Execution``); its state is kept in the memory of the service (``RunStore``) until it restarts, and every
change is published on NATS.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import contextlib
import json
import logging
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Coroutine
from typing import Any, TypeVar

import nats
from nova import api
from nova.core.gateway import ApiGateway
from wandelbots_api_client.v2_pydantic.exceptions import ApiException, NotFoundException

from routines.api import models
from routines.api.models import CommandRoutineRun, CommandRoutineRunState
from routines.errors import Conflict, InvalidPlan, NotFound, Rejected, Unreachable
from routines.controller_states import ControllerStates
from routines.execution import Execution, IOOnlyExecution, MotionExecution, StepFailed
from routines.ios import IOConditionTimedOut, IOs
from routines.layout import lay_out
from routines.plan import ExecutionPlan, IOOnlyPlan, MotionPlan, compile_plan, execution_plan
from routines.planning import Planner, api_message
from routines.trajectory_execution import StartRefused

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

T = TypeVar("T")


PREPARING = CommandRoutineRunState("PREPARING")
RUNNING = CommandRoutineRunState("RUNNING")
COMPLETED = CommandRoutineRunState("COMPLETED")
FAILED = CommandRoutineRunState("FAILED")
STOPPED = CommandRoutineRunState("STOPPED")
FINAL = (COMPLETED, FAILED, STOPPED)

# The robot's location in the run state is updated at most this often [s].
PROGRESS_INTERVAL = 0.1
# How long a stop waits for the execution to stop the run.
STOP_TIMEOUT = 10.0
_STOP_POLL_INTERVAL = 0.05


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RunFailure:
    """Why a run failed: the readable ``message`` and its typed ``cause``."""

    message: str
    cause: models.CommandRoutineFailureCause


class RunStore:
    """The runs of the service, in memory: a restart forgets them."""

    def __init__(self):
        self._runs: dict[str, CommandRoutineRun] = {}
        self._stops: dict[str, asyncio.Event] = {}
        self._failures: dict[str, RunFailure] = {}

    def _stop_event(self, run: str) -> asyncio.Event:
        return self._stops.setdefault(run, asyncio.Event())

    async def request_stop(self, run: str, failure: RunFailure | None = None) -> None:
        """Ask the execution of ``run`` to stop it: ``STOPPED``, or ``FAILED`` with ``failure`` as its error.

        The first request decides.
        """
        event = self._stop_event(run)
        if not event.is_set() and failure is not None:
            self._failures[run] = failure
        event.set()

    async def wait_for_stop(self, run: str) -> None:
        """Return once a stop of ``run`` was requested, also before this call."""
        await self._stop_event(run).wait()

    def stop_failure(self, run: str) -> RunFailure | None:
        """Why the requested stop fails ``run``; ``None`` for a stop that leaves it ``STOPPED``."""
        return self._failures.get(run)

    async def put(self, run: CommandRoutineRun) -> None:
        self._runs[run.run] = run.model_copy()

    async def get(self, run: str) -> CommandRoutineRun | None:
        stored = self._runs.get(run)
        return None if stored is None else stored.model_copy()

    async def all_runs(self) -> list[CommandRoutineRun]:
        return [run.model_copy() for run in self._runs.values()]


def _cause(error: BaseException) -> str:
    """The innermost message of an error raised from task groups."""
    error = _innermost(error)
    return str(error) or type(error).__name__


def _innermost(error: BaseException) -> BaseException:
    while isinstance(error, BaseExceptionGroup) and error.exceptions:
        error = error.exceptions[0]
    return error


def _failure_cause(error: BaseException) -> models.CommandRoutineFailureCause:
    """The ``CommandRoutineFailureCause`` of an error that failed a started run.

    A command that is not a motion fails on its IOs; everything else is the motion.
    """
    inner = _innermost(error)
    if isinstance(inner, StepFailed):
        timed_out = isinstance(inner.__cause__, IOConditionTimedOut)
        return models.CommandRoutineFailureCause("IOWaitTimedOut" if timed_out else "IOFailed")
    return models.CommandRoutineFailureCause("MotionFailed")


async def _first_of(**awaitables: Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]) -> str:
    """Run ``awaitables`` until the first one ends, cancel the others and return its name.

    Of several that end together, the one given first wins. Cancelling the execution closes
    its connection to the controller, which stops the motion. An error of the one that ends
    is raised.
    """
    tasks = {asyncio.ensure_future(awaitable): name for name, awaitable in awaitables.items()}
    try:
        done, _ = await asyncio.wait(tasks, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
    finally:
        for task in tasks:
            task.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)
    first = next(task for task in tasks if task in done)
    first.result()
    return tasks[first]


_ESTOP_CAUSE = "The run was ended by an emergency stop"
_ESTOP_REFUSAL = "The controller reports an emergency stop or another safety stop"
_ESTOP = models.CommandRoutineFailureCause("EmergencyStop")
# As the program runner: every other safety state stops the robot.
_SAFE_STATES = (api.models.SafetyStateType.SAFETY_STATE_NORMAL, api.models.SafetyStateType.SAFETY_STATE_REDUCED)


def _is_estop(state: api.models.RobotControllerState) -> bool:
    return state.safety_state not in _SAFE_STATES


def _activity(state: api.models.MotionGroupState) -> str | None:
    """What NOVA is doing with the motion group, if it is busy."""
    execute = state.execute
    if execute is None or execute.details is None:
        return None
    details = execute.details
    if isinstance(details, api.models.JoggingDetails):
        return "jogging is active"
    if isinstance(details.state, api.models.TrajectoryEnded):
        return None
    return f"trajectory '{details.trajectory}' is being executed"


class RunPublisher:
    """Publishes every change of a run on ``{instance}.v2.cells.{cell}.command-routines.runs.{run}``."""

    def __init__(self, client: nats.NATS | None, cell: str):
        self._client = client
        self._cell = cell

    def subject(self, run: str) -> str:
        return f"nova.v2.cells.{self._cell}.command-routines.runs.{run}"

    async def publish(self, run: CommandRoutineRun) -> None:
        if self._client is None:
            return
        if not self._client.is_connected:
            logger.warning(f"Run {run.run} ({run.state.root}) not published: NATS is not connected")
            return
        try:
            await self._client.publish(self.subject(run.run), run.model_dump_json(exclude_none=True).encode())
        except Exception:  # the run is in the store; a lost event must not fail the run
            logger.exception(f"Publishing run {run.run} failed")


def _now() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc)


def _location(run: CommandRoutineRun) -> float | None:
    return None if run.current_location is None else run.current_location.root


class _Report:
    """Writes what an execution does to its run in the store and publishes every change on NATS."""

    def __init__(self, store: RunStore, run: CommandRoutineRun, publisher: RunPublisher):
        self._store = store
        self._publisher = publisher
        self.run = run
        self.accepted = asyncio.Event()
        self.as_accepted = run
        self._progressed_at = 0.0
        self._latest: float | None = None
        self._held_back: asyncio.TimerHandle | None = None
        self._pending: asyncio.Future | None = None
        self._clean_ups: list[Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]] = []

    def when_ended(self, clean_up: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]) -> None:
        self._clean_ups.append(clean_up)

    async def clean_up(self) -> None:
        """What the execution left to do after the run ended, in the reverse order it was asked for."""
        for clean_up in reversed(self._clean_ups):
            try:
                await clean_up()
            except Exception:  # the run has ended; nothing to report it on
                logger.exception(f"Cleaning up after run {self.run.run} failed")

    async def started(self) -> None:
        await self._put()
        self.as_accepted = self.run.model_copy()
        self.accepted.set()

    async def at(self, command: int, location: float | None = None) -> None:
        """The run executes ``command``; the robot is at ``location``, if given (else where it last was).

        A new command is written at once; a new location at most every ``PROGRESS_INTERVAL``, and one held
        back goes out at the end of the interval.
        """
        now = asyncio.get_running_loop().time()
        if location is not None:
            self._latest = location
        moved = self._latest is not None and self._latest != _location(self.run)
        if (self.run.state, self.run.current_command_index) == (RUNNING, command):
            if not moved:
                return
            if now - self._progressed_at < PROGRESS_INTERVAL:
                if self._held_back is None:
                    delay = self._progressed_at + PROGRESS_INTERVAL - now
                    self._held_back = asyncio.get_running_loop().call_later(delay, self._write_held_back)
                return
        await self._write(command, now)

    def _write_held_back(self) -> None:
        """The location held back; only while the run is still at the command it was held back for."""
        self._held_back = None
        command = self.run.current_command_index
        if self.run.state == RUNNING and command is not None:
            self._pending = asyncio.ensure_future(self._write(command, asyncio.get_running_loop().time()))

    async def _write(self, command: int, now: float) -> None:
        if self._held_back is not None:
            self._held_back.cancel()
            self._held_back = None
        if self.run.started_at is None:
            self.run.started_at = _now()
        self.run.state, self.run.current_command_index = RUNNING, command
        if self._latest is not None:
            self.run.current_location = models.Location(self._latest)
        self._progressed_at = now
        await self._put()

    async def finish(self, state: CommandRoutineRunState, failure: RunFailure | None = None) -> None:
        """The run ends in ``state``; it keeps the command it was at and where the robot was."""
        if self._held_back is not None:
            self._held_back.cancel()
            self._held_back = None
        if self._pending is not None and not self._pending.done():
            self._pending.cancel()  # a held-back location must not write over the final state
            with contextlib.suppress(asyncio.CancelledError):
                await self._pending
        self.run.state = state
        if self._latest is not None:
            self.run.current_location = models.Location(self._latest)  # also one held back
        self.run.error = self._failure(failure)
        self.run.ended_at = _now()
        await self._put()

    def _failure(self, failure: RunFailure | None) -> models.CommandRoutineFailure | None:
        """The failure of a ``FAILED`` run: what went wrong, at the command it was at, and where the robot stopped."""
        if failure is None:
            return None
        return models.CommandRoutineFailure(
            code=models.CommandRoutineErrorCode("ExecutionFailed"),
            cause=failure.cause,
            message=failure.message,
            command_index=self.run.current_command_index,
            error_location_on_trajectory=self.run.current_location,
        )

    async def _put(self) -> None:
        await self._store.put(self.run)
        await self._publisher.publish(self.run)


class RunService:
    """Plans command routines, starts them and tracks their runs."""

    def __init__(self, gateway: ApiGateway, cell: str, nats_client: nats.NATS | None = None):
        self._gateway = gateway
        self._store = RunStore()
        self._cell = cell
        self._planner = Planner(gateway, cell)
        self._ios = IOs(gateway, cell, nats_client)
        self._states = ControllerStates(gateway, cell, nats_client)
        self._publisher = RunPublisher(nats_client, cell)
        self._tasks: set[asyncio.Task] = set()
        self._starting_or_running: set[str] = set()

    async def plan(
        self, routine: models.CommandRoutine, controller: str | None = None, motion_group_override: str | None = None
    ) -> models.PlanCommandRoutineResponse:
        """Plan ``routine`` for ``controller`` (and ``motion_group_override``, if given) without moving the robot."""
        layout = lay_out(routine, controller, motion_group_override)
        if layout.io_only:
            await self._check_controller(layout.controller)
        trajectory = await self._planner.plan(layout)
        # Triggers at a distance along the path need the TCP position of every sample.
        tcp_positions = (
            await self._planner.tcp_positions(layout, trajectory)
            if trajectory is not None and layout.needs_tcp_positions
            else None
        )
        return compile_plan(layout, trajectory, tcp_positions)

    async def list_runs(self) -> list[CommandRoutineRun]:
        """The runs since the service started."""
        return await self._store.all_runs()

    async def get(self, run: str) -> CommandRoutineRun:
        found = await self._store.get(run)
        if found is None:
            raise NotFound(f"Command routine run '{run}' not found")
        return found

    async def stop(self, run: str, failure: RunFailure | None = None) -> CommandRoutineRun:
        """Stop ``run`` and return it once it has stopped: ``STOPPED``, or ``FAILED`` with ``failure`` as its error.

        A run that already ended is returned unchanged.
        """
        found = await self.get(run)
        if found.state in FINAL:
            return found
        await self._store.request_stop(run, failure)
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        deadline = loop.time() + STOP_TIMEOUT
        while found.state not in FINAL and loop.time() < deadline:
            await asyncio.sleep(_STOP_POLL_INTERVAL)
            found = await self.get(run)
        return found

    async def start(
        self,
        request: models.StartCommandRoutineRunRequest,
        timeout_ms: int | None = None,
        disconnected: Callable[[], Awaitable[bool]] | None = None,
    ) -> CommandRoutineRun:
        """Start executing the plan of ``request`` on its controller and motion group, as it is: never planned again.

        An I/O-only plan addresses the ``CONTROLLER`` IOs of the request's controller. With ``timeout_ms`` the run
        is returned once it ended. It is stopped and fails when the time is up, or when ``disconnected`` tells
        that the caller is gone: a synchronous run never goes on without its caller.

        Raises:
            Rejected: Why the run cannot start. Nothing has moved or been written when it is raised.
        """
        match execution_plan(request):  # checked before any call to NOVA
            case IOOnlyPlan() as plan:
                await self._check_controller(plan.controller)
                run = await self._launch(IOOnlyExecution(plan, self._ios), plan, watched_controller=None)
            case MotionPlan() as plan:
                run = await self._start_motion(plan)
        if timeout_ms is None:
            return run
        return await self._await_end(run.run, timeout_ms, disconnected)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Stop tracking: runs still executing are interrupted."""
        for task in list(self._tasks):
            task.cancel()
        await asyncio.gather(*self._tasks, return_exceptions=True)

    async def _start_motion(self, plan: MotionPlan) -> CommandRoutineRun:
        motion_group = plan.motion_group
        # Two starts on this instance must not both pass the checks below.
        if motion_group in self._starting_or_running:
            raise Conflict(f"A command routine run is active on motion group '{motion_group}'")
        self._starting_or_running.add(motion_group)
        try:
            await self._check_motion_group_free(plan.controller, motion_group)
            execution = MotionExecution(plan, self._ios, self._gateway, self._states, self._cell)
            return await self._launch(
                execution,
                plan,
                watched_controller=plan.controller,
                on_end=lambda: self._starting_or_running.discard(motion_group),
            )
        except BaseException:
            self._starting_or_running.discard(motion_group)
            raise

    async def _check_controller(self, controller: str | None) -> None:
        """The controller an I/O-only routine or plan is given for its ``CONTROLLER`` IOs must exist.

        A motion routine's controller and motion group are checked when it is planned (``Planner.setup``), a plan's
        when its run starts (``_check_motion_group_free``).
        """
        if controller is None:
            return
        await _read(
            self._gateway.controller_api.get_robot_controller(cell=self._cell, controller=controller),
            not_found=f"Controller '{controller}' not found",
            what=f"controller '{controller}'",
        )

    async def _check_motion_group_free(self, controller: str, motion_group: str) -> None:
        """The controller is not in an emergency stop, the motion group exists, and nothing else drives it.

        Runs of other instances, programs and jogging all show in the motion group state.
        The controller rejects a second claim on the motion group as well.
        """
        controller_state = await _read(
            self._gateway.controller_api.get_current_robot_controller_state(cell=self._cell, controller=controller),
            not_found=f"Controller '{controller}' not found",
            what=f"controller '{controller}'",
        )
        if _is_estop(controller_state):
            raise Conflict(f"{_ESTOP_REFUSAL} on controller '{controller}' ({controller_state.safety_state.value})")
        state = await _read(
            self._gateway.motion_group_api.get_current_motion_group_state(
                cell=self._cell, controller=controller, motion_group=motion_group
            ),
            not_found=f"Motion group '{motion_group}' not found on controller '{controller}'",
            what=f"motion group '{motion_group}'",
        )
        activity = _activity(state)
        if activity is not None:
            raise Conflict(f"Motion group '{motion_group}' is busy: {activity}")

    async def _launch(
        self, execution: Execution, plan: ExecutionPlan, watched_controller: str | None, on_end=None
    ) -> CommandRoutineRun:
        """Start ``execution`` of ``plan`` in the background and return its run once the run was accepted.

        ``watched_controller``, the controller of a plan with motions, is watched for an emergency stop.
        """
        run = CommandRoutineRun(
            run=uuid.uuid4().hex,
            command_routine=plan.command_routine,
            dataset=plan.dataset,
            state=PREPARING,
            created_at=_now(),
        )
        report = _Report(self._store, run, self._publisher)
        task = self._track(self._execute(execution, report, watched_controller), name=f"run-{report.run.run}")
        if on_end is not None:
            task.add_done_callback(lambda _: on_end())
        accepted = asyncio.create_task(report.accepted.wait())
        try:
            await asyncio.wait({task, accepted}, return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED)
        finally:
            accepted.cancel()
        if not report.accepted.is_set():
            task.result()  # raises why the run was not accepted
            raise RuntimeError("The run ended before it was accepted")  # pragma: no cover
        return report.as_accepted

    async def _await_end(
        self, run: str, timeout_ms: int, disconnected: Callable[[], Awaitable[bool]] | None
    ) -> CommandRoutineRun:
        """``run`` once it ended; it fails when ``timeout_ms`` expires or when the caller disconnects first."""
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        deadline = loop.time() + timeout_ms / 1000
        found = await self.get(run)
        while found.state not in FINAL:
            if loop.time() >= deadline:
                return await self.stop(
                    run,
                    RunFailure(
                        f"The timeout of {timeout_ms} ms of the synchronous start expired",
                        models.CommandRoutineFailureCause("TimeoutExpired"),
                    ),
                )
            if disconnected is not None and await disconnected():
                logger.warning(f"Run {run}: the client of its synchronous start disconnected; the run is stopped")
                return await self.stop(
                    run,
                    RunFailure(
                        "The client of the synchronous start disconnected",
                        models.CommandRoutineFailureCause("ClientDisconnected"),
                    ),
                )
            await asyncio.sleep(min(_STOP_POLL_INTERVAL, max(deadline - loop.time(), 0)))
            found = await self.get(run)
        return found

    async def _execute(self, execution: Execution, report: _Report, controller: str | None) -> None:
        """Execute ``execution`` to its end, then clean up after it.

        What the execution left to clean up runs on its own once the run ended (or its start was refused), so it
        delays neither the final state nor a next run on the motion group.
        """
        try:
            await self._end(execution, report, controller)
        finally:
            self._track(report.clean_up(), name=f"clean-up-{report.run.run}")

    async def _end(self, execution: Execution, report: _Report, controller: str | None) -> None:
        """Run ``execution`` until it ends, is stopped, or ``controller`` reports an emergency stop; write how it ended.

        Raises:
            Rejected: Why the start is refused, when the run ended before it was accepted.
        """
        run = report.run.run
        watched: dict[str, Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]] = {
            "execution": execution.run(report),
            "stop": self._store.wait_for_stop(run),
        }
        if controller is not None:
            watched["estop"] = self._wait_for_estop(controller)
        try:
            ended = await _first_of(**watched)
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            if report.accepted.is_set():
                await report.finish(
                    FAILED,
                    RunFailure(
                        "The run was interrupted because the service stopped",
                        models.CommandRoutineFailureCause("ServiceStopped"),
                    ),
                )
            raise
        except Exception as error:  # every failure of a run is reported in its state
            if not report.accepted.is_set():
                raise _rejection(error) from error
            logger.exception(f"Command routine run {run} failed")
            failure = RunFailure(_cause(error), _failure_cause(error))
            # The controller may abort the motion before the e-stop shows in its state stream.
            if controller is not None and await self._is_estop(controller):
                failure = RunFailure(f"{_ESTOP_CAUSE}: {failure.message}", _ESTOP)
            await report.finish(FAILED, failure)
            return
        if not report.accepted.is_set():  # pressed between the check before the start and the acceptance
            raise Conflict(_ESTOP_REFUSAL)
        if ended == "stop":
            failure = self._store.stop_failure(run)
            await report.finish(STOPPED if failure is None else FAILED, failure)
        elif ended == "estop":
            await report.finish(FAILED, RunFailure(_ESTOP_CAUSE, _ESTOP))
        else:
            await report.finish(COMPLETED)

    def _track(self, coroutine: Coroutine[Any, Any, None], name: str) -> asyncio.Task:
        """Run ``coroutine`` in the background until it ends or the service closes."""
        task = asyncio.create_task(coroutine, name=name)
        self._tasks.add(task)
        task.add_done_callback(self._tasks.discard)
        return task

    async def _wait_for_estop(self, controller: str) -> None:
        """Return once the controller reports an emergency stop (or another safety stop)."""
        async with contextlib.aclosing(self._states.stream(controller)) as states:
            async for state in states:
                if _is_estop(state):
                    logger.info(f"Emergency stop on controller '{controller}': {state.safety_state}")
                    return
        await asyncio.Future()  # the stream ended: no e-stop seen, keep the run going

    async def _is_estop(self, controller: str) -> bool:
        try:
            state = await self._gateway.controller_api.get_current_robot_controller_state(
                cell=self._cell, controller=controller
            )
        except Exception:  # the run has failed already; its own error is reported
            logger.exception(f"Reading the state of controller '{controller}' failed")
            return False
        return _is_estop(state)


# How NOVA's HTTP refusals while a run starts are answered: a plan it cannot take is the caller's to fix, a
# controller in use is a conflict. Every other status (5xx, also 401/403: the service's own access) is NOVA failing.
_REFUSALS: dict[int, type[Rejected]] = {400: InvalidPlan, 422: InvalidPlan, 404: NotFound, 409: Conflict}


async def _read(awaitable: Awaitable[T], *, not_found: str, what: str) -> T:
    """``awaitable``, a read from NOVA before a run starts, with NOVA's errors as the refusals they mean."""
    try:
        return await awaitable
    except NotFoundException as error:
        raise NotFound(f"{not_found}: {api_message(error)}") from error
    except ApiException as error:
        raise Unreachable(f"Reading {what} failed: {api_message(error)}") from error
    except OSError as error:
        raise Unreachable(f"NOVA could not be reached: {error}") from error


def _rejection(error: BaseException) -> Rejected:
    """Why a run that failed before it was accepted is refused."""
    inner = _innermost(error)
    if isinstance(inner, Rejected):
        return inner
    if isinstance(inner, StartRefused):
        return Conflict(str(inner))
    if isinstance(inner, ApiException) and inner.status in _REFUSALS:
        return _REFUSALS[inner.status](f"The robot controller refused the run: {api_message(inner)}")
    return Unreachable(f"Starting the run failed: {_cause(inner)}")

339	                    if self._pausing:

342	            elif details is None and state.standstill:
343	                at_target = distance(list(state.joint_position), target_joints) <= ARRIVAL_JOINT_TOLERANCE
344	                has_run = running or leaves_target or loop.time() >= has_run_by
345	                if at_target and (has_run or self._pausing):
346	                    self._moved_to(target)
347	                    return True
348	                if self._pausing:
349	                    return False
350	                if running:
351	                    raise MotionInterrupted("The robot stopped before the target")
352	                # Not seen moving and not at the target: the motion has not started yet.
353	
354	    def _joints_at(self, location: float) -> list[float]:
355	        return joints_at(self._trajectory.joint_positions, self._trajectory.locations, location)
356	
357	    def _time_at(self, location: float) -> float:
358	        return time_at(self._trajectory.times, self._trajectory.locations, location)
359	
360	
361	def _rejection_message(error: api.models.AddTrajectoryError | None) -> str:
362	    """Why the controller does not take a trajectory: its message, the kind of error and where, as it reports them."""
363	    if error is None:
364	        return "The robot controller rejects the trajectory"
365	    kind = None if error.data is None else error.data.kind
366	    reason = "; ".join(part for part in (error.message, kind) if part) or "no reason given"
367	    where = "" if error.location is None else f" at location {error.location:.3f}"
368	    return f"The robot controller rejects the trajectory{where}: {reason}"
